newsitem.title: USA: Clinton fails to defuse criticism of Iraq policy.
newsitem.headline: Clinton fails to defuse criticism of Iraq policy.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Tuesday briefed key lawmakers on his strategy for discouraging Iraqi military action, but failed to defuse Republican criticism of his saber-rattling toward Baghdad.

"Saddam Hussein is far better off than he was two weeks ago. We judge success by results. The results are that he (Saddam) is better off, and we have basically done nothing except launch 44 cruise missiles," said Republican Sen. John McCain.

McCain, who has been one of the most outspoken critics of the president's policy, was referring to U.S. attacks on Iraqi air defense installations in southern Iraq on Sept. 3 following Iraqi attacks on Kurds in northern Iraq.

Clinton and other top administration officials, including Secretary of State Warren Christopher and Defense Secretary William Perry, briefed Republican and Democratic congressional leaders amid signs that chances of a further U.S. show of force in the Gulf were diminishing.

Sen. Joseph Lieberman, a Connecticut Democrat, said after the meeting that Clinton had signed an order Monday night to send 3,500 U.S. troops to Kuwait to reinforce 1,500 troops already there. Iraq can expect to be "hit and hit hard" if it offers further provocations, Lieberman said.
But a Pentagon spokesman said on Tuesday he did not expect U.S. infantry reinforcements to be sent to Kuwait at present because of an absence of new challenges from Iraq.
